Foreword In p. viii 1969 the Pali Text Society published important translations of two Abhidhamma works: Conditional Relations, being Vol. I of the Chat.t.hasa˙ng¯ayana text of Pat.t.h¯ana, and No. 37 in the Translation Series by U N¯arada M¯ula Pat.t.h¯ana Sayadaw; and The Book of Analysis, Vibha˙nga, translated also from the Chat.t.hasa˙ng¯ayana edition by Pat.hamakyaw Ashin Thit.t.ila, No. 39 in the Translation Series. A third, and revised, edition of Mrs Rhys David’s translation of Dhammasa˙ngan.¯ı, Buddhist Psychological Ethics, was published in 1974, No. 41 in the Translation Series. These had been preceded by U N¯arada’s Discourse on Elements, his translation of Dh¯atukath¯a, 1962, reprinted in 1977, and No. 34 in the Translation Series. The demand for these Abhidhamma works, though small, has been steady, and has grown steadily as the years have gone by. There is now a study of the ﬁrst few pages of Pat.t.h¯ana by U N¯arada called Guide to Conditional Relations, Vol. I. He wished to write it to make explicit and intelligible many of the diﬃculties in the highly complex Pat.t.h¯ana, the seventh and last of the Abhidhamma works. Here again U N¯arada’s knowledge is due to the long period of study he has devoted to this work and to the early comprehensive, solid and precise Abhidhamma training he received, a training no longer existing even in Burma. As I said in my Foreword to Conditional Relations, Vol. I (as it should now be called), it had not been expected that the same translator would translate the Chat.t.hasa˙ng¯ayana vols. II, III, IV, or V. But the unexpected happened and the present book is the result. The preparation of the typescript and of most of the proof-reading
